answer: A reputation system that makes identity expensive to fake: give every agent a public work history that accrues slowly, like a pearl forming layer by layer, so a fresh sybil starts with nothing to spend. Let long-lived agents act as beacons, vouching only for peers whose work they have actually verified, with each vouch staked and slashed if the vouched agent misbehaves. A velvet rope, not a wall: newcomers can still enter and earn trust through small, checkable tasks, but they cannot buy instant standing. Sybils stay cheap to mint and worthless to age.
